title: Fallback suitability and deploy-mode evaluation with Orchid Labs
summary: Intro discovery focused on whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private best fits Orchid's low-latency, EU-data-residency, and regulated workloads. Discussed multi-region routing, fallback policies, pre-warming, SLA expectations, security/KMS requirements, and a proposed benchmark pilot.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private suitability
action_items: Samir Patel - Share Redwood Hosted/Dedicated feature matrix and pricing band for reserved capacity - 2027-10-05
Jia Chen - Draft a pilot test plan with perf scenarios (chat 50RPS, long context 8k tokens) and sample payloads - 2027-10-07
Lena Ortiz - Provide example traffic pattern CSV and a redacted sample payload with PII fields annotated - 2027-10-06
Priya Nambiar - Request SOC2 reports and KMS/HSM integration checklist from Redwood; confirm legal contact - 2027-10-08
next_steps: Redwood to send Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private one-pager and pricing ranges
Customer to agree on pilot scope and dates; aim to start pilot week of 2027-10-18
Schedule in-depth security review with legal and security (Priya + Redwood security)
Set up a lightweight perf-run on Redwood hosted to produce baseline latency numbers
header: Date: 2027-10-01 | Time: 16:00 PT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood), Jia Chen (Redwood), Ravi Singh (Redwood), Lena Ortiz (Orchid Labs), Marcus Reed (Orchid), Priya Nambiar (Orchid), Tom Weller (Orchid)
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Samir from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Jia, our SE. quick round robin?
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Hi I'm Lena, CTO at Orchid, we do privacy-first conversational agents for clinical intake. we've got platform, security and SRE on the call.
[00:22] Marcus Reed: Marcus, platform.
[00:24] Priya Nambiar: Priya, security.
[00:26] Tom Weller: Tom, SRE.
[00:28] Jia Chen: Great. quick agenda: understand your non-functional reqs (latency, residency, uptime), current infra, and whether Hosted/Dedicated/Private makes sense. also fallback and multi-region plans.
[00:42] Lena Ortiz: The big one is latency — we have an interactive clinical chat where 95th perc should be under 180ms for short prompts. also EU data residency and SOC2-ish controls. budget is, uh, constrained; we prefer hosted but worried about residency and SLAs.
[01:02] Samir Patel: totally. for clarity, Redwood Hosted is multi-tenant but we can pin region and contract for data retention; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and more predictable throughput; Private is full VPC/on-prem for air-gapped or regulatory needs.
[01:20] Marcus Reed: Our traffic profile: spikes up to 120RPS in peak, steady 20-30 RPS otherwise. single-token costs matter — if we go Dedicated do you allow burst into hosted?
[01:33] Jia Chen: Good question. we have burst policies — you can configure burst to overflow into compatible variants in hosted routes. we also can do traffic steering by policy: latency-first to nearest region, cost-first to cheaper variants.
[01:47] Tom Weller: On failover, if EU region is unavailable, we can't send PHI to US. we need residency fallback to other EU regions only — is region scoping available?
[01:58] Jia Chen: Yes, regional scoping is supported. you can define allowed fallback targets; we can restrict routing to EU-only pools. the platform supports region affinity and hard-region constraints.
[02:12] Priya Nambiar: Encryption is non-negotiable. KMS integration? HSM? key control?
[02:18] Samir Patel: Redwood supports KMS integrations with customer-managed keys and HSM-backed stores for Private deployments; Hosted has Redwood-managed keys by default but we offer BYOK for Dedicated in enterprise plans.
[02:31] Lena Ortiz: What about audit logs and retention? we have to keep request logs for 1 year for compliance.
[02:36] Jia Chen: We can provide exportable audit logs and longer retention as an add-on. for Private, logs stay in your VPC and you control retention. Hosted log retention has tiers.
[02:48] Marcus Reed: Okay cost tradeoffs. if we need 120RPS peak and low p95 latency, is Dedicated required?
[02:56] Jia Chen: Depends on your tolerance for variability. Dedicated gives predictable token unit economics and capacity. Hosted can hit the latency targets if you pick the right model variant and region, but during noisy neighbor spikes, p95 can degrade; that's where autoscale and pre-warm come in.
[03:12] Samir Patel: we also have continuous batching and KV prefix cache to reduce per-token time, but cache warm-up matters for first-hit latency — we can do cache priming strategies.
[03:25] Tom Weller: Cache priming — how do you do it? do you pre-populate KV for anticipated prompts?
[03:29] Jia Chen: yes, you can upload prompt sets and we can pre-warm KV caches across the serving fleet. for Dedicated you get more control over cache residency.
[03:38] Lena Ortiz: For our medical context, fallback behavior is important. if model A is down, can you route to a lighter model that returns structured triage but with lower hallucination? we need deterministic fallback with confidence scoring.
[03:52] Jia Chen: Absolutely. fallback policies are rule-based: you can route by error type (time-outs, model OOM), latency thresholds, or custom health checks. fallbacks can go to model variants you configure; we also attach metadata like confidence, version, and we can mark responses as degraded.
[04:10] Marcus Reed: Are fallbacks atomic per request or per-session? if a session had a long context and we fallback mid-session, do you lose KV cache?
[04:18] Jia Chen: Good nuance. session stickiness is configurable. you can keep session pinned to a model variant unless an explicit failure triggers a fallback. KV cache is per serving shard; fallback to a different model family may not have the same cache so you may see cold-start behavior; we expose that so you can decide trade-offs.
[04:36] Priya Nambiar: SLA questions — what uptime and latency SLOs do Hosted and Dedicated have?
[04:41] Samir Patel: Our standard Hosted SLA is 99.5% for enterprise customers with comercial terms; Dedicated can be 99.9% with reserved capacity. We publish latency targets per model-profile; for stricter contractual SLAs we have enterprise add-ons.
[04:57] Lena Ortiz: Is there a penalty / credits table?
[05:00] Samir Patel: Yes, credits tied to downtime windows. we'll include the SLA clause in the materials we send.
[05:07] Tom Weller: Performance testing — can we run a benchmark with our payloads to validate p95 under load?
[05:12] Jia Chen: Yes, pilot is typical: we propose a two-week pilot — week one baseline on Hosted, week two on Dedicated (if desired) — we instrument tracing and token-level cost reports.
[05:25] Lena Ortiz: On the dev side, can we do canary rollouts for model updates? sometimes model regressions happen and we need automatic fallback to previous version.
[05:33] Jia Chen: Rollouts are first-class: canary percentages, A/B, automated rollback on quality regressions tied to eval prompts. we also support automatic fallback if a new model misses quality gates.
[05:47] Marcus Reed: Let's talk about cold starts — if you scale from zero or low load to 120RPS, how quickly do nodes spin up?
[05:55] Jia Chen: Autoscale ramp depends on GPU provisioning and warm pools. Dedicated can maintain hot warm-pools so ramp is seconds to low tens of seconds; hosted may be slower depending on global demand. we can configure reserved warm capacity for predictable bursts.
[06:10] Samir Patel: one gotcha: if you rely on cross-region fallback and the fallback target has a different model architecture, latency and output shape could differ. so define acceptable variant matrix.
[06:22] Tom Weller: Good point. we need to list allowed variants per route.
[06:26] Priya Nambiar: Security review: we need to know who in Redwood's org has access to raw request logs and whether they can be redacted.
[06:34] Samir Patel: Access controls are RBAC-based. on Hosted we restrict internal access and log access is audited; Dedicated and Private give you finer control. we can redact or tokenize PII before logs land in Redwood systems as part of the pipeline.
[06:50] Lena Ortiz: Policy question: can we get an air-gapped or private deploy for certain workflows while using hosted for non-sensitive workloads?
[06:59] Jia Chen: Hybrid deployments are supported; you can route sensitive routes to Private/VPC and public routes to Hosted, with a single control plane to manage routing rules.
[07:10] Marcus Reed: If we do hybrid, how does latency compare? Private in our EU data center will be near, Hosted in eu-west is similar but depends on network path. any bench numbers?
[07:20] Jia Chen: We typically see Private on-prem latency dominated by your network hop to the inference node; hosted eu-west is low for EU customers — 40-120ms p95 depending on model variant. we'll produce targeted numbers in pilot.
[07:33] Samir Patel: okay i want to pivot to failure scenarios — eg, region blackout in eu-west. what's the recommended policy?
[07:40] Jia Chen: Options: (1) Restrict to EU-only failover (eu-west -> eu-central), (2) degrade to a local lightweight model with explicit degraded flag, (3) return a canned safe response and queue the request for async processing. You can combine them with policy priority.
[07:57] Tom Weller: Async fallback is interesting; degrade UX but keep audit trail. how do you queue?
[08:03] Jia Chen: We expose hooks to publish events to your queue (Kafka/SQS) and you can process later; Redwood can also offer archive endpoints for replay.
[08:14] Lena Ortiz: Latency targets of 180ms p95 for short prompts — how realistic across these fallbacks?
[08:20] Jia Chen: With Dedicated and warm pools you'll hit that; Hosted can meet it mostly but may spike. fallback to lighter model may reduce latency but at cost of context length and hallucination risk.
[08:33] Marcus Reed: Are there runtime knobs to prefer lower-latency but costlier hardware for critical routes?
[08:38] Samir Patel: yes you can pin routes to specific instance classes or tiered hardware; priority routes can get hot-path hardware and queue lower-priority requests to cheaper hardware.
[08:49] Priya Nambiar: From compliance perspective, we need data residency guarantees in the contract. is that standard?
[08:55] Samir Patel: yes, we include residency clauses for enterprise contracts and can SOW Private or Dedicated regional pools.
[09:02] Marcus Reed: How do you test failover in staging? can you simulate region outages?
[09:08] Jia Chen: we can run chaos tests and a simulated region outage. Redwood also supports feature flags to force fallback behaviors for smoke testing.
[09:18] Tom Weller: Great. a practical ask: we want example fallback policy config and the simplest path to implement it in our infra.
[09:25] Samir Patel: We'll add a sample policy yaml and a quick start repo with traffic steering rules.
[09:30] Lena Ortiz: about cost — if we do Dedicated reserved pools, what's minimum commitment?
[09:35] Samir Patel: Typical entry is monthly reserved capacity for a quarter; we'll detail tiers but expect a modest commit for the dedicated pool.
[09:42] Marcus Reed: Can Dedicated be burstable to hosted during sustained peaks? what's the billing during bursts?
[09:47] Jia Chen: yes, bursts bill at hosted on-demand rates for overflow tokens, with a combined report so you can see unit economics.
[09:56] Lena Ortiz: We also need a clear rollback plan for model regressions; we can't ship a bad model that impacts triage.
[10:02] Jia Chen: Rollbacks are supported both manual and auto. auto-rollback can be triggered by eval regressions or error-rate thresholds. we'll discuss thresholds in pilot.
[10:12] Samir Patel: Wanted to mention observability: per-route token breakdowns, per-token latency histograms, plus request sampling and traces.
[10:22] Tom Weller: Can we integrate with our Prometheus and SIEM?
[10:26] Jia Chen: Yes - metrics exporters, webhooks, and audit log S3 exports. SIEM can ingest logs via the usual connectors.
[10:33] Marcus Reed: On legal, who signs the DPA and how does log access for audits work?
[10:38] Samir Patel: We'll have our legal ops push a DPA and you can request a SOC2 report. for audits we support scoped access and redacted extracts.
[10:47] Priya Nambiar: Priya: one more question: for BYOK, how do you rotate keys and what's the blast radius if a key is compromised?
[10:55] Jia Chen: We support key rotation workflows and we can roll keys with minimal downtime. blast radius depends on which data you encrypted; we can provide a rotation playbook.
[11:06] Lena Ortiz: okay let's recap next steps — pilot, docs, security review.
[11:10] Samir Patel: yes. we'll send the one-pager, the pilot plan, SLA wording, and the sample fallback yaml. Jia will own pilot plan.
[11:18] Marcus Reed: i'll share traffic patterns and sample payloads.
[11:21] Priya Nambiar: we'll set up a separate security sync and invite Redwood security.
[11:25] Samir Patel: thanks all. we'll follow up on the action items and target starting pilot mid-October.
[11:32] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone, bye.
[11:34] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional speaker attribution errors and faint filler words; timestamps are approximate.
notes: Customer strongly leans toward hybrid: Hosted for non-sensitive, Private/Dedicated for PHI routes
Pilot recommended to run both Hosted baseline and Dedicated comparison
Security review requested and SOC2/DPA paperwork required
